To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we synthesized a series of sildenafil analogues and found that two of them (10 and 12) are extremely potent inhibitors of mushroom tyrosinases.
ten new sildenafil analogues were synthesized, and that the most‐potent tyrosinase inhibitory compound was found to be compound 10, with an IC50 value of 3.59 μM.
we developed new sildenafil analogues that possess tyrosinase‐inhibitory properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of sildenafil analogues possessing tyrosinase inhibitory activity.
the design and synthesis of sildenafil analogues possessing tyrosinase inhibitory activity and the development of new, effective drugs for the treatment of melanin‐related skin disorders.

the development of novel, effective, and selective mushroom tyrosinases inhibitors, and with the discovery of new, potent, and selective melanogenesis inhibitors, which could be used for the development of novel drugs for the treatment of skin disorders such as vitiligo, freckles, melasma, and other pigmentation disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of the methyl ether group in the pyrazole moiety is essential for the observed inhibitory effect of compounds 10 and 15, whereas the presence of the hydroxy group is crucial for that of compound 12.

the introduction of the 4‐ethoxysulfonamide group into the 4‐position of 3‐(7,8‐dihydroxy‐1‐methylene‐1,3,8‐tripropyl‐1H,8H‐pyrazino[2,3‐f]quinolin‐5‐yl)-benzenesulfonic acid amide (1), which is the main active ingredient of the well‐known drug sildenafil (Viagra),
, in general, the introduction of the methyl ether group in the 7‐position of sildenafil is beneficial for the tyrosinase‐inhibiting activity of these analogues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the methyl ether analogues 6‐15 of sildenafil (Viagra®, 1) possess a high tyrosinase inhibitory potential and, therefore, could serve as potential candidates for the treatment of skin disorders.

the methyl ether analogues 10 and 15 are the best tyrosinase inhibitory agents among the sildenafil analogues synthesized so far, and are the most‐active tyrosinase‐inhibiting agents reported in the literature.
we synthesized and tested the first sildenafil‐based compounds with potential tyrosinase inhibitory activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the introduction of a methyl ether moiety into the sildenafil molecule is an effective strategy to enhance the tyrosinase inhibitory potential of sildenafil analogues.
the introduction of a hydroxyl or sulfhydryl group into the 4′‐position of sildenafil is a promising way to enhance the inhibitory effect of sildenafil on the enzyme tyrosinase.

the introduction of a sulfonamide group at C‐3 of the pyrazolopyrimidine moiety of 1, and the replacement of the hydroxyl group of 1 by a hydroxyethyl group, is a very efficient strategy for the design of new tyrosinase‐inhibiting sildenafil analogues.
